evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Every licensed kitchen has hours it sits empty.' is an observation addressed to kitchens; the lede ('Ovenhour rents them out... A small food maker books a shift') makes what/who clear, and the two buttons 'I make food and need a kitchen' / 'I run a kitchen with empty hours' route each side. As a maker I only find myself in the lede and button, not the headline.
evidence.fit: Both audiences get a path (#makers form, ovenhour.example/kitchens with a 'have these to hand' checklist), county variation gets its own section with six concrete things that differ, and 'no listings' is stated on the board and sample listing. But the brief says there is nothing yet for makers; the page invents a maker waiting list ('Email me when a kitchen lists', status grid 'Makers: Waiting list open') that is really a mailto draft, so the maker side's real state is not reflected in what the action does.
evidence.distinctiveness: Dark 'hour board' with three kitchen types (bakery 14, dinner restaurant 15, caterer 19 empty hours), a sample listing laid out as a document with kitchen notes on the left and maker notes on the right, and a 'One shift, by the clock' two-column table. These come from the product; the serif/tile palette is calm and specific. Hero itself is a plain left-aligned headline with an empty right half.
evidence.proof: The sample listing (Weeknight shift 10 pm-5 am, equipment, not included, house rules) is good evidence of what a maker gets, but it starts below the first screens (about 1100px down at 1440) and is entirely static. The hour board only animates; nothing responds to clicks. As a kitchen owner I can't see what listing my hours would feel like.
evidence.craft: 1440 first screen: right half of the hero is empty space beside a 15ch headline. probe: axe color-contrast 1 node at 390/1440; 6 text elements at 11.84px at 390. 768: axis labels '6 pm' and '12 am' crowd at the right edge of the board. Otherwise consistent spacing and a deliberate serif/sans pairing.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow, nav wraps to a row of small text links (about 20px tall, no menu), CTAs 45px tall. Tapping 'I make food and need a kitchen' scrolls about 5,900px to the form. Board rows restack name/count above track and stay readable; hour chips in the form are 38px tall.
evidence.honesty: Samples are well labelled ('Sample listing.' notice, 'Sample / Not a real kitchen' tag, '$— per hour set by the kitchen', board caption 'Typical patterns... not listings'). But the maker form's fine print 'One email when there's something near you. Nothing else.' implies a subscription; after submit at 1440/768/390 it says 'Noted. We'll email maker@test.example when a kitchen lists hours near Durham, Durham County' while the only thing that happened is a mailto draft opening to makers@ovenhour.example (an address the brief did not supply). The status grid repeats 'Waiting list open'.
evidence.interaction: Form: empty submit shows 'We need an email address we can reach and the city and county you cook in.' but focuses the City field, not Email (script checks indexOf('email')===0 on 'an email...'). Bad email shows a specific error; chips toggle. Valid submit hides the form and shows a success box regardless of whether the mail was sent. The board and listing have no controls. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Written in the trade's words: 'write them the way you'd say them to a new hire', 'If a piece of equipment isn't listed, it isn't yours for the night', 'leaves the morning crew nothing to notice'. Some repetition between the listing side notes and the by-the-clock table; the clock table describes booking features ('Sees who has booked') in present tense.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: headline, lede and two audience buttons; only the top bakery row of the board shows at the bottom edge. 390: headline, lede, buttons, board legend just visible; no artifact. Button labels name who you are, not what happens when you click.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Kitchens close at ten. Licenses don't.' is a slogan that needs a second read, but the subhead immediately says 'a booking site where licensed commercial kitchens rent their empty hours to small food makers... a maker books one shift and sees exactly what comes with it'. Each button has a line beside it saying what happens ('Sign-up is open now. No maker can book yet...'; 'No account. Your note goes to the founders' inbox with your county on it.').
evidence.fit: Resolves the 'two websites stapled together' tension with one example sheet and a 'Read as: the kitchen / a maker' toggle that relabels the same panel ('Makers may use' becomes 'You get', 'House rules' becomes 'You agree to'). Kitchen path goes to the supplied ovenhour.example/kitchens; maker path is an honest note, matching 'nothing yet for makers'. County section says launch counties aren't chosen and permit plus county sit on each listing. Pricing section says Ovenhour's fee is not set and kitchen sign-up costs nothing. Thin on what the kitchen owner worries about next (who the maker is, insurance).
evidence.distinctiveness: The weekly roster with service blocks, amber listed blocks and dashed 'held' blocks is specific to this product, as are the step fragments ('fryer: off limits', 'Thu 22:00-06:00 · 8 h'). The hero is a familiar split headline/subhead layout and later sections are standard bands.
evidence.proof: 1440: the example sheet with 'EXAMPLE LISTING' stamp, the Read-as toggle and Mon-Wed rows is in the first viewport. Operated: kitchen mode starts '9 blocks · 76 h' (24+5x8+12 = 76, consistent); holding Tue gives '8 blocks · 68 h'; maker mode on Sun shows 'Sun 18:00-06:00 · 12 h' and '12 h × $38 = $456 at the illustrative price'. Every number is labelled illustrative.
evidence.craft: Clean type scale and consistent spacing at 1440/768/390; axe reports no violations and no text under 12px. Minor: the light-grey 06:00-09:00 slivers on Tue-Sat are not explained by the legend (listed/service/held), and the service tooltip says 'Dinner service 09:00-21:30'. Mono 12px labels are small.
evidence.mobile: 390: Menu button opens a nav (aria-expanded true), tapping 'County rules' scrolls there and closes the menu. CTAs are full width with the disclosure line under each. Sheet stacks with day labels above full-width bars and stays usable, but blocks are 30px tall (under 44), and after tapping Sun in maker mode the result line sits about 180px below the tapped block. The sheet's grid starts below the first screen at 390.
evidence.honesty: Labels sit where the material appears: 'Example listing', 'hours, equipment and price are illustrative', 'Price per hour, illustrative: $38', footer 'Nothing on this page is a review, a booking count or a partner.' The maker action says before the click 'It opens as an email to the founders; nothing is stored here.' Small issues: 'Ovenhour is a booking site' is present tense, and makers@ovenhour.example is not an address the brief supplied.
evidence.interaction: Operated at all three widths: Read-as toggle switches labels and kicker; clicking a block in kitchen mode toggles listed/held and updates totals; held blocks are inert in maker mode; keyboard Space on a focused block toggles it (7 blocks · 60 h). Empty form submit shows native 'Please fill out this field.'; valid submit shows 'Opening your mail app...' plus a copyable preformatted note under the button. No console errors. No explicit reset, though every toggle is reversible.
evidence.copy: Specific and in the trade's register: 'Mark the hours you are dark', 'The equipment list is the contract', 'Counts and sizes, not brands. Two ovens means two ovens.', 'Book one block, not a month.' Button text says what happens ('Send the founders your shift'). The headline wordplay is the one line a stranger may not parse.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific outcome for both audiences, two actions with what-happens text, and the labelled example sheet with the interactive toggle and roster in view. 390: headline, subhead and both actions with disclosures are in view, and only the 'EXAMPLE LISTING' card header shows at the bottom; the roster itself needs a scroll.

problems: At 390 the roster blocks are 30px tall and the panel that answers a tap sits below the tapped block, sometimes off-screen.
The maker form is tucked inside the county section and sends to makers@ovenhour.example, which the brief did not supply; no field for the hours the maker wants beyond a blank line in the email body.
Headline is a clever slogan rather than a plain promise, and the roster has an unexplained grey band and a 'Dinner service 09:00' mislabel.

reason: As both the kitchen owner and the maker, B shows me my side of the same listing in the first screen and lets me operate it, and every action says what will really happen before I click; as the founder I could put it live tomorrow. A has stronger long-form copy and a better county section, but its maker form tells visitors they are on a list that does not exist, which I would not publish under my name. I would change my mind only if A's maker confirmation were rewritten to disclose the mail draft before submit and B's interactive sheet proved confusing to real kitchen owners.
